# Anchor Phenomenon

::: {.anchor-box}
## 🌀 It Has Felt Like Storms Are Getting Worse

[**Does the data support that feeling, and will it continue?**]{.driving-question}

In recent years, powerful storms have battered communities across the United States. From deadly blizzards burying the Northeast under feet of snow to Category 5 hurricanes devastating coastal cities, it *feels* like extreme weather is getting worse. But science doesn't run on feelings—it runs on **evidence**.

In this unit, you will investigate whether storms really are becoming more frequent and intense, and use climate models to argue what the future may hold for your community.
:::

# Unit Driving Question

::: {.phenomenon-box}
### Will there be more frequent and more intense severe storms in the future?

This question will guide your work across all four lesson sequences in this unit. By the end, you will construct an evidence-based argument about how climate change may alter storm patterns in your region.
:::

# Tell the Story

Before analyzing data and building models, two real events anchor what this unit is about. Watch each video and examine the data that follows — **jot down observations, what surprises you, and the questions you want answered**.

---

## 🌨️ Tell the Story: Blizzards

Every few years, a massive winter storm bears down on the East Coast, shutting down cities and threatening lives. The news report below captures that moment of anticipation and dread right before one such storm arrives. As you watch, consider: *Where is this storm heading? Who is in danger? Does this event seem unusual or part of a pattern?*

### 📊 NYC Seasonal Snowfall: 2014–2024 (2018–19 & 2019–20 Highlighted)

The bar chart below shows **NYC's total seasonal snowfall** for each winter from 2014 to 2024. The two seasons that match your storm track maps are highlighted in blue.

```{ojs}

  {season: "2017–18", total: 40.9, highlight: false},
  {season: "2018–19", total: 20.5, highlight: true},
  {season: "2019–20", total: 4.8,  highlight: true},
  {season: "2020–21", total: 38.6, highlight: false},
  {season: "2021–22", total: 10.3, highlight: false},
  {season: "2022–23", total: 20.7, highlight: false},
  {season: "2023–24", total: 8.5,  highlight: false}
]

Plot.plot({
  title: "NYC Seasonal Snowfall (2014–2024)",
  subtitle: "Blue bars = seasons matching your storm track maps",
  width: 700,
  height: 360,
  x: { label: "Season", tickRotate: -25 },
  y: { label: "Total Snowfall (inches)", domain: [0, 60], grid: true },
  marks: [
    Plot.barY(winterSeasons, {
      x: "season", y: "total",
      fill: d => d.highlight ? "#1565c0" : "#90caf9",
      tip: true
    }),
    Plot.ruleY([25], { stroke: "#555", strokeDasharray: "6,4" }),
    Plot.text([{season: "2022\u201323", y: 27}], {
      x: "season", y: "y", text: d => "\u224825\" historical avg", fill: "#555", fontSize: 11
    })
  ]
})
```

## 🌀 Tell the Story: Tropical Storms

In September 2017, Hurricane Maria struck Puerto Rico as a Category 4 storm — one of the deadliest hurricanes in recorded US history. Years later, communities were still rebuilding. The video below documents the devastation. As you watch, consider: *What made this storm so catastrophic? How does geography matter? Is this a rare event or part of a pattern?*

```{ojs}
{
  const topojson = await require("topojson-client@3");
  const world = await fetch("https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2/land-50m.json").then(r => r.json());
  const land = topojson.feature(world, world.objects.land);
  const tracks = hurrYear === "2018" ? hurricaneTracks2018 : hurricaneTracks2020;
  const seasonLabel = hurrYear === "2018"
    ? "2018 — 15 named storms, 8 hurricanes, 2 major"
    : "2020 — 30 named storms, 13 hurricanes, 6 major (record)";

  return Plot.plot({
    title: `Atlantic Hurricane Season ${hurrYear}`,
    subtitle: seasonLabel,
    width: 750,
    height: 440,
    projection: {
      type: "equirectangular",
      domain: { type: "MultiPoint", coordinates: [[-100, 5], [0, 48]] }
    },
    color: {
      legend: true,
      domain: ["TD","TS","H1","H2","H3","H4","H5"],
      range: ["#6ec6ff","#00bcd4","#ffeb3b","#ff9800","#ff5722","#e91e63","#9c27b0"],
      label: "Category"
    },
    marks: [
      Plot.geo(land, { fill: "#2d5016", stroke: "#1a3009", strokeWidth: 0.5 }),
      Plot.geo({ type: "Sphere" }, { stroke: "#444", fill: "#1b263b" }),
      Plot.geo(land, { fill: "#2d5016", stroke: "#1a3009", strokeWidth: 0.5 }),
      ...tracks.map(t =>
        Plot.line(t.points, {
          x: d => d[0], y: d => d[1],
          stroke: catColor(t.cat),
          strokeWidth: t.cat.startsWith("H") ? 2.5 : 1.5,
          strokeOpacity: 0.85,
          curve: "catmull-rom"
        })
      ),
      ...tracks.map(t =>
        Plot.dot([t.points[0]], {
          x: d => d[0], y: d => d[1],
          r: 3, fill: catColor(t.cat), stroke: "#000", strokeWidth: 0.5
        })
      ),
      ...tracks.map(t =>
        Plot.text([t.points[t.points.length - 1]], {
          x: d => d[0], y: d => d[1],
          text: [t.name], fill: "#fff", fontSize: 8,
          dx: 8, dy: -4, fontWeight: 600
        })
      )
    ]
  });
}
```

# What Makes This Unit Different?

This unit builds directly on **Unit 4: Climate Change**, where you analyzed data about Earth's changing climate. Now you'll apply that understanding to a question that hits close to home: **how might climate change affect the storms that impact your city?**

Instead of memorizing weather vocabulary, you'll:

- 🔬 **Build models** of how storms form
- 📊 **Analyze real data** on storm frequency and intensity
- 🗺️ **Read weather maps** like a meteorologist
- 💬 **Construct arguments** about future climate impacts

## 🌥️ Global Cloud Cover by Season

Where the atmosphere is most active, you see clouds. Three patterns drive almost everything in this unit: the **Intertropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)**, **mid-latitude storm tracks** (where blizzards live), and **monsoon systems**. All three shift with the seasons — and that shift is exactly why hurricane season and blizzard season fall when they do.

Toggle through the four seasons and look for:
- Where cloud cover is **thickest** (most active storms / deepest convection)
- Which latitudes are **clearest** (subtropical deserts, sinking air zones)
- How the cloud bands connect to **when and where** hurricanes and blizzards strike

```{=html}
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/topojson-client@3/dist/topojson-client.min.js"></script>

<div style="max-width:920px; margin:30px auto; font-family:system-ui,sans-serif;">

  <!-- Season tab buttons -->
  <div style="display:flex; gap:10px; margin-bottom:10px; justify-content:center; flex-wrap:wrap;">
    <button id="cbtn-DJF" onclick="showCloudSeason('DJF')" style="padding:8px 20px;border-radius:999px;border:none;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;font-size:13px;background:#1565c0;color:#fff;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(21,101,192,0.4);">❄️ DJF — Winter</button>
    <button id="cbtn-MAM" onclick="showCloudSeason('MAM')" style="padding:8px 20px;border-radius:999px;border:none;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;font-size:13px;background:#e0e0e0;color:#555;">🌱 MAM — Spring</button>
    <button id="cbtn-JJA" onclick="showCloudSeason('JJA')" style="padding:8px 20px;border-radius:999px;border:none;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;font-size:13px;background:#e0e0e0;color:#555;">☀️ JJA — Summer</button>
    <button id="cbtn-SON" onclick="showCloudSeason('SON')" style="padding:8px 20px;border-radius:999px;border:none;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;font-size:13px;background:#e0e0e0;color:#555;">🍂 SON — Fall</button>
  </div>

  <!-- Season description -->
  <div id="cloud-info" style="background:#f0f4ff;border-left:5px solid #1565c0;padding:12px 16px;border-radius:0 10px 10px 0;font-size:0.92em;line-height:1.6;margin-bottom:10px;min-height:56px;"></div>

  <!-- Map canvas -->
  <div style="border-radius:16px;overflow:hidden;box-shadow:0 15px 35px rgba(0,0,0,0.2);position:relative;background:#1b4f8c;">
    <canvas id="cloud-map" width="900" height="450" style="display:block;width:100%;"></canvas>
    <div id="cloud-map-loading" style="position:absolute;top:50%;left:50%;transform:translate(-50%,-50%);color:rgba(255,255,255,0.9);font-weight:700;font-size:15px;text-shadow:1px 1px 4px rgba(0,0,0,0.8);pointer-events:none;">Loading map…</div>
  </div>

  <!-- Legend -->
  <div style="display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:10px;margin-top:12px;font-size:12px;font-weight:600;color:#555;">
    <span>Clear sky</span>
    <div style="width:200px;height:14px;border-radius:7px;background:linear-gradient(to right,#2a6096,rgba(255,255,255,0.95));border:1px solid #bbb;"></div>
    <span>Dense clouds</span>
  </div>
  <p style="text-align:center;font-size:0.78em;color:#888;margin-top:6px;">
    Modeled seasonal climatology (ISCCP/MODIS) · Equirectangular projection — all regions visible simultaneously
  </p>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  var CLOUD_SEASON_INFO = {
    DJF: { color: '#1565c0', label: '❄️ December–January–February (Northern Winter)',
      desc: '<strong>Blizzard season.</strong> North Atlantic and Pacific storm tracks are at peak strength (40–65°N) — this is when nor\'easters and blizzards hammer the US East Coast. The ITCZ sits near or just south of the equator. Subtropical deserts are at their driest and clearest.' },
    MAM: { color: '#2e7d32', label: '🌱 March–April–May (Northern Spring)',
      desc: '<strong>Transition season.</strong> Mid-latitude storm tracks weaken as the temperature contrast between poles and tropics decreases. The ITCZ migrates northward. Blizzard risk drops rapidly. The Atlantic hurricane season hasn\'t started yet.' },
    JJA: { color: '#e65100', label: '☀️ June–July–August (Northern Summer)',
      desc: '<strong>Monsoon + early hurricane season.</strong> The South Asian and West African monsoons produce some of the heaviest cloud cover on Earth. The ITCZ is at its northernmost extent. Atlantic hurricane season begins — warm tropical oceans fuel developing storms. NH mid-latitude storm tracks are at minimum.' },
    SON: { color: '#6a1b9a', label: '🍂 September–October–November (Northern Fall)',
      desc: '<strong>Peak hurricane season + blizzard ramp-up.</strong> September is historically the most active month for Atlantic hurricanes — the Caribbean and Gulf of Mexico are very active. Mid-latitude storm tracks strengthen again as winter returns.' }
  };

  var _worldLand = null;
  var _currentSeason = 'DJF';

  // ── Cloud fraction model (lat-row base + fast pixel corrections) ──────────

  function cfRowBase(lat, S) {
    var b = 0.50;
    var itczLat = { DJF: -5, MAM: 4, JJA: 10, SON: 3 }[S];
    b += 0.40 * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((lat - itczLat) / 9,  2));
    var nhLat  = { DJF: 56, MAM: 52, JJA: 57, SON: 54 }[S];
    var nhStrg = { DJF: 0.27, MAM: 0.20, JJA: 0.11, SON: 0.22 }[S];
    b += nhStrg * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((lat - nhLat) / 11, 2));
    b += 0.24   * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((lat + 52)   / 10, 2)); // Southern Ocean
    var nhSub = { DJF: 25, MAM: 27, JJA: 30, SON: 27 }[S];
    b -= 0.20   * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((lat - nhSub) / 8,  2)); // NH subtropical dry
    b -= 0.17   * Math.exp(-0.5 * Math.pow((lat + 25)   / 8,  2)); // SH subtropical dry
    if (S === 'DJF' && lat > 65) b -= 0.10; // Arctic winter dry
    if (lat < -75)               b -= 0.10; // Antarctic plateau
    return b;
  }

  function cfPixel(lat, lng, S, base) {
    var cf = base;
    if (lat >  12 && lat <  35 && lng >  -10 && lng <  58)  cf -= 0.22; // Sahara / Arabian
    if (lat >  22 && lat <  38 && lng > -118 && lng < -100)  cf -= S === 'DJF' ? 0.04 : 0.14; // SW USA / Baja
    if (lat > -32 && lat < -16 && lng >  -76 && lng <  -65)  cf -= 0.18; // Atacama
    if (lat > -35 && lat < -16 && lng >  114 && lng <  145)  cf -= 0.14; // Australian outback
    if (S === 'JJA' && lat >  5 && lat <  30 && lng >  65  && lng <  130) cf += 0.32; // S Asian monsoon
    if (S === 'JJA' && lat >  5 && lat <  20 && lng > -18  && lng <   30) cf += 0.25; // W African monsoon
    if (S === 'JJA' && lat > 20 && lat <  40 && lng >  110 && lng <  145) cf += 0.17; // E Asian Meiyu
    if (S === 'SON' && lat >  0 && lat <  20 && lng >   65 && lng <  115) cf += 0.18; // monsoon retreat
    if ((S === 'JJA' || S === 'SON') && lat > 8 && lat < 22 && lng > -100 && lng < -60) cf += 0.18; // Caribbean
    if (S === 'JJA' && lat > 25 && lat < 42 && lng > -130 && lng < -120) cf += 0.18; // CA marine stratus
    if (lat > -28 && lat <  -3 && lng >  -84 && lng <  -72)  cf += 0.19; // Humboldt / Peru stratus
    if (lat > -28 && lat < -10 && lng >    7 && lng <   18)  cf += 0.17; // Benguela stratus
    if ((S === 'DJF' || S === 'SON') && lat > 40 && lat < 65 && lng > -50 && lng < -10) cf += 0.10; // N Atlantic belt
    return Math.max(0.06, Math.min(0.92, cf));
  }

  // ── Draw topojson geometry onto canvas 2D ctx ────────────────────────────

  function drawGeo(ctx, W, H, feature) {
    var geom = (feature && feature.geometry !== undefined) ? feature.geometry : feature;
    if (!geom) return;
    function rings(poly) {
      poly.forEach(function (ring) {
        ring.forEach(function (pt, i) {
          var x = ((pt[0] + 180) / 360) * W;
          var y = ((90 - pt[1]) / 180) * H;
          if (i === 0) ctx.moveTo(x, y); else ctx.lineTo(x, y);
        });
        ctx.closePath();
      });
    }
    if      (geom.type === 'MultiPolygon')    geom.coordinates.forEach(rings);
    else if (geom.type === 'Polygon')         rings(geom.coordinates);
    else if (geom.type === 'GeometryCollection') geom.geometries.forEach(function (g) { drawGeo(ctx, W, H, { geometry: g }); });
    else if (feature.type === 'FeatureCollection') feature.features.forEach(function (f) { drawGeo(ctx, W, H, f); });
  }

  // ── Full map render ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  function drawCloudMap(season) {
    var canvas = document.getElementById('cloud-map');
    if (!canvas) return;
    var ctx = canvas.getContext('2d');
    var W = canvas.width, H = canvas.height;

    // 1. Ocean background
    var grad = ctx.createLinearGradient(0, 0, 0, H);
    grad.addColorStop(0,   '#0a2e5e');
    grad.addColorStop(0.5, '#1b4f8c');
    grad.addColorStop(1,   '#0a2e5e');
    ctx.fillStyle = grad;
    ctx.fillRect(0, 0, W, H);

    // 2. Land masses
    if (_worldLand) {
      ctx.fillStyle   = '#3d6b2a';
      ctx.strokeStyle = '#2a4d1a';
      ctx.lineWidth   = 0.4;
      ctx.beginPath();
      drawGeo(ctx, W, H, _worldLand);
      ctx.fill();
      ctx.stroke();
    }

    // 3. Cloud alpha layer (ImageData — no cross-origin, no CORS)
    var imgd = ctx.createImageData(W, H);
    var px   = imgd.data;
    for (var row = 0; row < H; row++) {
      var lat  = 90 - (row / H) * 180;
      var base = cfRowBase(lat, season);
      for (var col = 0; col < W; col++) {
        var lng  = (col / W) * 360 - 180;
        var cf   = cfPixel(lat, lng, season, base);
        var a    = Math.round(Math.pow(Math.max(cf - 0.10, 0) / 0.90, 0.65) * 220);
        var i4   = (row * W + col) * 4;
        px[i4]   = 255; px[i4+1] = 255; px[i4+2] = 255; px[i4+3] = a;
      }
    }
    // blit via an offscreen canvas — saves on reflow
    var cc = document.createElement('canvas');
    cc.width = W; cc.height = H;
    cc.getContext('2d').putImageData(imgd, 0, 0);
    ctx.drawImage(cc, 0, 0);

    // 4. Reference latitude lines
    var refLines = [
      { lat:  66.5, label: 'Arctic Circle (66.5°N)',      color: 'rgba(200,230,255,0.65)', dash: [4,3] },
      { lat:  23.5, label: 'Tropic of Cancer (23.5°N)',   color: 'rgba(255,230,140,0.75)', dash: [6,4] },
      { lat:   0,   label: 'Equator',                     color: 'rgba(255,255,255,0.85)', dash: []    },
      { lat: -23.5, label: 'Tropic of Capricorn (23.5°S)',color: 'rgba(255,230,140,0.75)', dash: [6,4] },
      { lat: -66.5, label: 'Antarctic Circle (66.5°S)',   color: 'rgba(200,230,255,0.65)', dash: [4,3] }
    ];
    ctx.font = '10px system-ui,sans-serif';
    refLines.forEach(function (ref) {
      var y = Math.round((90 - ref.lat) / 180 * H) + 0.5;
      ctx.setLineDash(ref.dash);
      ctx.strokeStyle = ref.color;
      ctx.lineWidth   = ref.dash.length ? 0.8 : 1.3;
      ctx.beginPath(); ctx.moveTo(0, y); ctx.lineTo(W, y); ctx.stroke();
      ctx.setLineDash([]);
      ctx.fillStyle = ref.color;
      ctx.fillText(ref.label, 4, y - 3);
    });
  }

  // ── Button / info panel update + redraw ───────────────────────────────────

  window.showCloudSeason = function (season) {
    _currentSeason = season;
    var colors = { DJF: '#1565c0', MAM: '#2e7d32', JJA: '#e65100', SON: '#6a1b9a' };
    ['DJF','MAM','JJA','SON'].forEach(function (s) {
      var btn = document.getElementById('cbtn-' + s);
      if (!btn) return;
      var col = colors[s];
      btn.style.cssText = (s === season)
        ? 'padding:8px 20px;border-radius:999px;border:none;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;font-size:13px;background:' + col + ';color:#fff;box-shadow:0 2px 8px rgba(0,0,0,0.25);'
        : 'padding:8px 20px;border-radius:999px;border:none;cursor:pointer;font-weight:700;font-size:13px;background:#e0e0e0;color:#555;';
    });
    var si   = CLOUD_SEASON_INFO[season];
    var info = document.getElementById('cloud-info');
    if (info) { info.innerHTML = '<strong>' + si.label + '</strong><br/>' + si.desc; info.style.borderColor = si.color; }
    drawCloudMap(season);
  };

  // ── Init: draw immediately, load land in background ────────────────────

  function waitForTopojson(cb) {
    if (typeof topojson !== 'undefined') { cb(); return; }
    setTimeout(function () { waitForTopojson(cb); }, 80);
  }

  waitForTopojson(function () {
    // Show clouds first (no land yet)
    window.showCloudSeason('DJF');
    var loading = document.getElementById('cloud-map-loading');
    if (loading) loading.textContent = '';

    // Load land outlines, then redraw with them
    fetch('https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/world-atlas@2/land-110m.json')
      .then(function (r) { return r.json(); })
      .then(function (world) {
        _worldLand = topojson.feature(world, world.objects.land);
        drawCloudMap(_currentSeason);
      })
      .catch(function () { /* silently continue without land outlines */ });
  });
})();
</script>
```

# Connecting to Unit 4

In Unit 4, you learned that:

- Human activities have increased atmospheric CO₂ from 280 ppm to over 420 ppm
- This enhanced greenhouse effect is raising global temperatures
- Positive feedback loops (ice-albedo, water vapor, permafrost) amplify warming
- Climate models project continued warming throughout the 21st century

::: {.check-understanding}

# What You'll Figure Out

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

| Sequence | You Will Figure Out... |
|----------|----------------------|
| **Blizzards** | Wind is caused by uneven heating → pressure differences. Cold and warm air masses collide to produce precipitation. Mid-latitude cyclones become blizzards under certain conditions. |
| **Storm Paths** | Global winds driven by uneven solar heating drive storm trajectories. Wind patterns may shift as temperatures rise. |
| **Hurricanes** | Hurricanes get energy from warm ocean water. Ocean temperature seasonality explains hurricane season. |
